paragraphs: Nayoti. In [Shabbat 121b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.121b.8) he killed a snake on Shabbat. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.121b.8.1) explains that he was Jewish and was called after his place.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The supplied Hebrew has כשבת in both the reference and the description of the act. The English reads them according to context, first “in Shabbat” and then “on Shabbat.”

In the linked incident, a creature falls into the study hall and Nayoti kills it. The surrounding discussion concerns snakes and scorpions. Rashi calls Nayoti Jewish and explains the name as a place designation. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2710&lang=en) specifies Nayot in Ramah.
